newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina,France,Senegal, Macau in ombudsmen pact.
newsitem.headline: Argentina,France,Senegal, Macau in ombudsmen pact.

text.p: Argentina's ombudsman said he signed technical cooperation and information exchange deals with his colleagues from France, Senegal, Sudan and Macau.

"The agreements will allow us to exchange technicians, documents and to communicate through Internet," Argentine ombudsman Jorge Maiorano said in a press release issued during a conference of the International Ombudsman Institute (IOI).

"In talks with Macau's and Sudan's ombusdsmen we detected they have the same problems we have -- their economies are opening up and consumers many times find themselves deprived not only of an advantageous situation, but also of an equal footing vis-a-vis utility companies.
"They expressed interest in knowing what do we do to prevent monopolistic companies from rising rates and we want to check opinions to know whether what we are doing is correct," he said.
Maiorano said he expects cooperation with the French ombudsman will help him to maximize his office's efficiency.
Ombudsmen, who first appeared as government officials in Scandinavia, generally investigate citizens' complaints about government actions, including state-owned enterprises.
Depending on the country, thier purview can cover such areas as human rights violations, poor management and complaints over public services. Often their judgments are non-binding.
More than 100 ombudsmen from 82 nations Thursday were wrapping up a four-day international conference of the IOI, an organization which holds such a meeting every four years.
